Total number of questions — 20
Regional disparities of States
*121. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the regional disparities of
different States are widening;
(b) whether as per statistics prepared
by the Central Statistical Organisation,
Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil
Nadu and West Bengal together account
for 42.5 per cent of aggregate State domestic
product, while Orissa, Bihar and a few other
States' share has far declined in 2003-04 at
1993-94 price level;
(c) whether it is because of the fact that
the new economic policy of Government
hardly had the scope for practising welfare
economics in these backward and poverty-
stricken States; and
(d) if so, what is the action plan of
Government to address this issue?
TRAI's direction to private companies
*122. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether TRAI has given any
direction to private telecom companies to
immediately discontinue "misleading" tariff
plans and show all monthly fixed recurring
charges under one subhead for transparency
to subscribers; and
(b) if so, the details of the direction given
by TRAI?
Framework to resolve Indo-China
border dispute
*123. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:

39
(a) whether India and China have agreed
to proceed towards a framework for
resolving vexed border dispute in a fair and
reasonable manner keeping in view political
perspective of overall bilateral relations;
(b) whether during the month of
September, talks on two sides reviewed in
a satisfactory manner, progress made in
Special Representatives' meeting and agreed
to proceed from political perspective of
overall bilateral relations;
(c) if so, at what stage border dispute is
at present and by what time clear picture
of settlement is being reached; and
(d) whether both Governments are
confident to settle this issue immediately
for improvement of relations between the
two countries?
Jaleswar-Chandneswar-Digha road
*124. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to declare
Jaleswar-Chandneswar-Digha road as a
National Highway in view of its importance
to link tourist centres; and
(b) if so, the progress made, so far?
Six laning of Golden Quadrilateral
*125. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government would shortly
roll out a mega Rs. 175,000 crore project
for six-laning of the entire 'Golden
Quadrilateral' network for complete
execution on build-operate-transfer basis;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) the funds allocation for this purpose
during the current Five Year Plan;
(d) the progress achieved in this
direction, so far;
(e) whether Government would build
the project on the public private-
partnership model;
(f) if so, the ratio thereof; and
(g) whether Government had set any
time-frame to complete this mega project?
SAARC Summit
*126. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Indian delegation led by
the Prime Minister participated in the 13th
SAARC Summit held on 12th November,
2005 in Dhaka;
(b) if so, the detail of discussions/
outcome of decisions taken at the said
meeting;
(c) whether the Indian delegation put
forward before the SAARC meeting any
specific suggestions; and
(d) if so, the reaction of member nations
to India's suggestion for a united bid to
combat terrorism with "zero tolerance"
towards cross-border terror?
Sale of excess coal to end-users
*127. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that at present
the selling of excess coal produced in
captive mines of core sector consumers to
other needy end-users is not legally feasible;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether a proposal to allow captive
coal mine companies to sell excess coal to

40
eligible end-users, is under consideration
of Government; and
(d) if so, the measures being taken by
Government to achieve this objective?
Denial of sophisticated technology
*128. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that developed
nations are denying sophisticated
technology to India

Training activities by KVIC
890. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRA-
IAH: Will the Minister of AGRO AND
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the training activities
provided by Khadi and Village Industries
Commission (KVIC) during the current
year, State-wise;
(b) the details of loan, subsidies
provided by KVIC during the current year
for proposals on the State of Andhra
Pradesh; and
(c) the details of loan default cases for
projects approved by KVIC in the above
State during the last two years?
Trade fairs in rural areas
891. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposed to
organise trade fairs in rural areas for
extension of agro and rural industries in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the names of districts to organise trade fairs
during the current financial year, State-wise;
and
(c) the funds required for organising
these fairs in districts selected for the
purpose and the manner in which these
funds are proposed to be mobilised?
PMRY in Assam
892. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be
pleased to state:
(a) the total loan disbursed by the banks
under the PMRY in Assam since 2000-01
till date, bank-wise, year-wise;
(b) whether any irregularity has been
noticed in disbursement of loan;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the action taken by Government
against the defaulters?

203
Khadi units in Rajasthan
893. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of units established
in Rajasthan by Khadi and Village Industries
Commission during the existing plan period;
(b) the employment generated thereby;
(c) whether any target has been fixed to
set up new industries in Rajasthan, during
the remaining period of Tenth Plan; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Separation of nuclear facilities
894. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is any proposal for
separation of nuclear facilities as civil and
military;
(b) if so, the details including the reason
for above separation and the present status
of the proposal;
(c) if so, whether there is any proposal
to allow private/marketing forces in civil
nuclear programme; and
(d) the share of nuclear energy in the
total power generation and power
utilization scenario of the country as on
today, State-wise, category-wise?
Export of nuclear power reactors
895. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the  PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that international
market has opened up for India for the export
of low-cost small and medium size nuclear
power reactors in the light of the US co-
operation in the nuclear energy sector;
(b) if so, what the NPCI is aiming to do
in the existing new and favourable scenario
to sell India's small sized nuclear reactors
to the world; and
(c) the tentative cost in developing a
SMR in India in comparison to China?
New nuclear power stations
896. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have given clearance to four sites for nuclear
power stations as the technology flow from
Indo-US deal on nuclear power is expected
to come through; and
(b) if so, the details of the four locations
cleared and the pre-project activities?
Lifting of ban on export of dual-use
Nuclear technology
897. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Canada, like
USA and UK, has lifted ban on export of
dual-use nuclear technology to India;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the likely share of Canada for co-
operation in our nuclear programme and
the projects likely tso be covered during
the next three years?
Increase of power generation capacity
